  9|나는 가죽옷을 뚫고 들어오는 혹한의 추위에 몸을 부르르 떨었다. 한서불침(寒暑不侵)은 개뿔이, 한서매우침이다.

101|“그때로 돌아가고 싶구나. 나른한 정오, 내리쬐는 햇살. 먹음직스럽게 걸어가는 황구…….”
102|
103|먹음직스러운 황구는 또 뭐야.
104|
105|동물보호단체가 기함할 소리를 한 궁기방의 눈꺼풀이 천천히 아래를 향해 내려갔다.

107|이 자식이 설마?

109|“야, 야!”

111|나는 황급히 녀석의 몸에 열양지기를 흘려보냈다.
112|
113|이렇게라도 정신을 차려야…….
114|
115|“따뜻하구나…….”
116|
117|“아니, 잠에서 깨라고 이 미친놈아!”
118|
119|철썩! 철썩!
120|
121|틀렸다. 아무리 뺨을 때려도 한 번 감긴 눈은 떠질 기미가 보이지 않았다.
122|
123|나는 계속해서 열양지기를 흘려보내며 외쳤다.
124|
125|“거기 누구 없어요! 한 명만 빨리 와 봐!”
126|
127|내 처절한 외침에 저 멀리서 한 사람이 다다다 달려왔다.
128|
129|“은인! 은인!”
130|
131|“나이스 청풍! 빨리 이 녀석 데리고 밖으로…….”
132|
133|바람처럼 달려온 청풍이 환하게 웃으며 손에 든 것을 내밀었다.
134|
135|“은인, 이것 보세요! 제가 처음으로 만든 눈사람이에요!”

145|망태기 안의 약초를 모두 확인한 신의가 고개를 끄덕였다.
146|
147|“이 정도면 충분하오.”

153|- 연계 퀘스트, [한빙지 약초 노예]를 성공적으로 완료했습니다!

155|- 업적, [지옥에서 살아 돌아온 심마니]를 달성했습니다!
156|
157|- 업적 달성으로 보너스 포인트를 10 획득했습니다!
158|
159|
160|
161|업적 제목 꼬라지 봐라. 이제 화낼 힘도 없다.
162|
163|지칠 대로 지친 우리의 모습을 바라보던 신의의 시선이 문득 한 사람에게 멈췄다.
164|
165|“청풍 공자는 왜 그리 상심해 있는 것이오?”
166|
167|그거야 청풍이 처음으로 만든 눈사람을 내가 화염신장으로 부숴 버렸기 때문이지.
168|
169|아직도 시무룩한 청풍을 죽일 듯이 노려본 나는 신의에게 물었다.
170|
171|“그럼 이걸로 준비는 끝난 겁니까?”
172|
173|“그렇소. 이 정도 양이라면 후에 무슨 일이 벌어져도 대비할 수 있을 거요.”
174|
175|“대비, 요?”
176|
177|신의가 무겁게 고개를 끄덕였다.
178|
179|“무슨 일이 벌어질지 모르오.”
180|
181|나는 잠시 잊고 있던 사실을 깨달았다. 신의는 지금껏 단 한 번도 ‘확신’한 적이 없었다는 것을.
182|
183|그저 가능성을 보았고, 최선을 다하겠다고 했을 뿐이다.
184|
185|‘끝날 때까지 끝난 게 아니다.’
186|
187|위기에 처할 때마다 스스로에게 속삭이던 그 말이, 지금 비수가 되어 가슴을 찔렀다.
188|
189|결국 내가 할 수 있는 말은 한 가지밖에 없었다.
190|
191|“최선을, 최선을 다해 주십시오.”
192|
193|“이 늙은이가 할 수 있는 모든 것을 다하겠소. 약속하지.”
194|
195|신의의 옆에 서 있던 문경이 힘주어 말했다.
196|
197|“저 역시 스승님의 곁에서 힘껏 돕겠습니다.”
198|
199|“고맙다.”
200|
201|“뭘요. 의생으로서 마땅히 해야 할 일인 걸요.”
202|
203|“그럼 본격적인 치료는 언제부터 시작하는 겁니까?”
204|
205|가만히 뭔가를 생각하던 신의가 입을 열었다.
206|
207|“아마도 칠 주야 후가 될 거요. 그때까지 나와 문경은 공자들이 가져온 스물네 종류의 약초를 한데 뭉치고 다듬어, 활신대법(活新大法)에 들어갈 재료로 쓸 것이오.”
208|
209|“그걸 전부 말입니까?”
210|
211|“이것도 일부에 불과하오. 다행히 활신대법에 필요한 나머지 재료는 갖고 있어 시간을 단축할 수 있었던 것이지.”
212|
213|“활신대법이 도대체 뭐길래…….”
214|
215|신의가 새하얀 수염을 쓰다듬으며 대답했다.
216|
217|“일전에 말한 적 있듯이 스승님께서도 한때 무림인이셨소. 주로 민초들을 상대로 의술을 베푸셨지만, 기(氣)를 어떻게 다스려야 하는지에 대해서도 매우 조예가 깊으셨지.”
218|
219|그 말을 듣자 얼추 짚이는 구석이 있었다.
220|
221|옆에 있던 혁무진이 탄성과 함께 불쑥 끼어들었다.
222|
223|“무림인! 무림인들을 치료하기 위해 만든 것이 활신대법이군요.”
224|
225|“그렇소. 기환노사(奇幻老師)도 그중 한 사람이었지. 활신대법 덕분에 심각한 주화입마에서 회복한 그분은 기문진을 설치해 주고 떠났소.”
226|
227|무림인에게 있어 주화입마는 사형 선고나 다름없다. 공력이 역류하며 기혈이 꼬이고 온갖 혈도와 단전을 망가트리기 때문이다.
228|
229|사람의 내부에서 작은 폭탄이 터졌다고 하면 이해가 빠를까.
230|
231|‘그런데 주화입마를 고쳤다니.’
232|
233|신의가 심각하다고 할 정도면 당시의 기환노사는 산송장이나 다름없는 상태였을 것이다.
234|
235|이야기만 들어도 활신대법의 효과가 어느 정도인지 알 것 같았다.
236|
237|‘그럼 노야도 분명히…….’
238|
239|나는 자연스럽게 이어지려는 생각을 훌훌 털어냈다.
240|
241|구태여 지금 확신할 이유도, 걱정할 필요도 없다.
242|
243|“잘 부탁드리겠습니다.”
244|
245|“대법의 준비가 끝나는 동안 그 누구도 환자가 있는 곳에 접근해서는 아니 되오. 아시겠소?”
246|
247|“예.”
248|
249|“그때 활신대법의 준비가 끝나고, 환자의 상태에 대해서도 더 명확히 알게 될 테니 참고 기다리시구려.”
250|
251|“명심하겠습니다.”
252|
253|“기억하시오, 칠 주야 후요.”
254|
255|그러나 신의의 말은 지켜지지 못했다.
256|
257|그가 문경과 함께 다시 모습을 드러낸 것은 고작 사흘이 지난 후였고, 나는 두 사람의 표정을 보자마자 직감할 수 있었다.
258|
259|“……무슨 일입니까.”
260|
261|한참의 침묵이 흐른 끝에 입을 연 것은, 신의가 아닌 문경이었다.
262|
263|“무형지독(無形至毒).”
264|
265|“뭐?”
266|
267|“환자의 신체 내부에 정체를 알 수 없는 극독이 있습니다. 그게 진짜 이유였어요.”
268|
269|“잠, 잠깐만.”
270|
271|머릿속이 뒤죽박죽 얽히고 꼬인다.
272|
273|난데없이 무형지독이라니. 나는 혼란스러운 눈빛으로 신의를 바라봤다.
274|
275|“이게 무슨 말입니까?”
276|
277|“들은 그대로요.”
278|
279|신의가 사흘 전과 비교도 할 수 없을 만큼 수척해진 얼굴로 말을 이었다.
280|
281|“대법을 준비하며 환자의 용태를 살피던 도중 이상한 점을 발견했소. 바로 더욱 기승을 부려야 할 열양지기가 조금씩 수그러들고 있다는 점이었지.”
282|
283|“그럼 오히려 잘된 것 아닙니까? 갑자기 독이라니, 그게 무슨…….”
284|
285|“아직 대법을 시행하지도 않았거늘, 어찌 열양지기가 홀로 줄어든단 말이오?”
286|
287|“그건…….”
288|
289|“혹 이상한 점을 느끼지 못했소?”
290|
291|그 순간, 문득 어떤 생각이 뇌리를 스쳤다.
292|
293|나는 하남에서 사천으로 오는 도중 틈틈이 적천강의 기운을 진기도인으로 안정시켰는데, 그런 시도와는 반대로 적천강의 열양지기는 점점 줄어들었다.
294|
295|‘단순히 쇠약해져 간다고만 생각했는데.’
296|
297|딱딱하게 굳은 내 표정에 신의가 한숨을 내쉬었다.
298|
299|“한 기운이 득세하면 반대편의 기운은 점점 작아지기 마련이오. 하나 환자의 경우는 달랐소. 음한지기는 그대로인데, 열양지기는 미세하게 줄어들고 있었지.”
300|
301|“그게…… 독 때문이란 말입니까?”
302|
303|“어찌 된 영문인지는 모르나, 환자의 몸에는 나로서도 감히 손댈 수 없는 무형지독이 숨어 있었소. 천운인지, 불행인지. 때마침 폭주한 열양지기가 무형지독을 감싸 이독제독(以毒制毒)의 역할을 하지 않았더라면 진즉 한 줌 혈수(血水)로 녹아내렸을 거요.”
304|
305|“……!”
306|
307|신의가 무형지독이라 부르는 그것이 언제, 어떻게 적천강에게 흘러들어 왔는지는 모른다.
308|
309|그러나 열양지기가 방파제가 되어 독의 확산을 막고 있다는 것만큼은 확실히 알아들었다.
310|
311|“그럼, 그럼 대법으로도 치료가 불가능한 겁니까?”
312|
313|“활신대법은 기운을 다스리고 얽힌 기혈을 풀 수 있으나, 저런 무형지독을 해독(解毒)하기에는 역부족이오. 만약 이대로 대법을 시행한다면…… 열양지기는 진정되겠지만 독을 막을 방법이 없소.”
314|
315|내가 다급하게 외쳤다.
316|

If the Master of Strange Illusions had suffered qi deviation severe enough for the Divine Physician to describe it that way, he must have been little more than a walking corpse at the time.

[P106]
Just hearing the story gave me some idea of how effective the Life-Restoring Great Technique was.

[P107]
*Then Old Master will definitely—*

[P108]
I quickly shook off the thought before it could finish forming.

[P109]
There was no reason to be certain yet, nor any need to worry.

[P110]
“Please take good care of him.”

[P111]
“Until preparations for the technique are complete, no one may approach the place where the patient is being kept. Do you understand?”

[P112]
“Yes.”

[P113]
“By then, the Life-Restoring Great Technique will be ready, and we should have a clearer understanding of the patient’s condition. Please wait patiently until then.”

[P114]
“I’ll keep that in mind.”

[P115]
“Remember. Seven days and nights.”

[P116]
But the Divine Physician was unable to keep his word.

[P117]
He reappeared with Mungyeong after only three days, and the moment I saw their expressions, I knew something had happened.

[P118]
“…What is it?”

[P119]
After a long silence, it was Mungyeong—not the Divine Physician—who finally spoke.

[P120]
“Formless Ultimate Poison.”

[P121]
“What?”

[P122]
“There is an unidentified, extremely deadly poison inside the patient’s body. That was the true cause.”

[P123]
“W-Wait.”

[P124]
My thoughts twisted into a chaotic knot.

[P125]
Formless Ultimate Poison? Out of nowhere?

[P126]
I looked at the Divine Physician in confusion.

[P127]
“What does that mean?”

[P128]
“Exactly what you heard.”

[P129]
Looking incomparably more haggard than he had three days earlier, the Divine Physician continued.

[P130]
“While preparing the technique and monitoring the patient’s condition, I discovered something strange. The Scorching Yang Qi, which should have been growing more rampant, was gradually subsiding.”

[P131]
“Then isn’t that a good thing? What does some sudden poison have to do with—”

[P132]
“We have not even performed the technique yet. How could the Scorching Yang Qi be decreasing on its own?”

[P133]
“That…”

[P134]
“Did you not notice anything strange?”

[P135]
At that moment, a thought flashed through my mind.

[P136]
During our journey from Henan to Sichuan, I had periodically stabilized Jeok Cheongang’s qi with True Qi Guidance. Yet despite my efforts, his Scorching Yang Qi had continued to diminish.

[P137]
*I thought he was simply growing weaker.*

[P138]
The Divine Physician sighed when he saw my expression harden.

[P139]
“When one type of energy gains the upper hand, the opposing energy naturally diminishes. But the patient was different. His Yin-Cold Qi remained unchanged, while his Scorching Yang Qi was gradually dwindling.”

[P140]
“Are you saying that was because of the poison?”

[P141]
“I do not know how it happened, but a Formless Ultimate Poison lies hidden within the patient’s body—one that even I would not dare touch. Whether by great fortune or terrible misfortune, the rampaging Scorching Yang Qi happened to envelop the Formless Ultimate Poison and counteract it like poison against poison. Otherwise, he would have melted into a handful of bloody liquid long ago.”

[P142]
“…!”

[P143]
I didn’t know when or how the poison the Divine Physician called Formless Ultimate Poison had entered Jeok Cheongang’s body.

[P144]
But I understood one thing clearly: the Scorching Yang Qi was acting as a breakwater, holding back the spread of the poison.

[P145]
“Then… does that mean even the technique can’t cure him?”

[P146]
“The Life-Restoring Great Technique can regulate his qi and untangle his disrupted qi and blood, but it is not enough to detoxify a poison like this. If we perform the technique as things stand… the Scorching Yang Qi will be calmed, but there will be nothing left to stop the poison.”

[P147]
I shouted urgently, “I’ll find an antidote! The Sichuan Tang Clan is here, isn’t it?”

[P148]
“…Young Master.”

[P149]
The Divine Physician shook his head, his expression dark.

[P150]
“I know very well that the Sichuan Tang Clan is the greatest authority under heaven when it comes to poison. But this poison…”

[P151]
His voice trailed off, and my heart seemed to drop into my stomach.

[P152]
*Even the Sichuan Tang Clan isn’t enough?*

[P153]
Damn it. This was a truly fucking awful situation.

[P154]
Right now, Jeok Cheongang had two savage wolves inside his body, each keeping the other in check.

[P155]
If either one disappeared, the other would regain its freedom and run wild.

[P156]
And now there was no way to detoxify the poison.

[P157]
*This is so fucked…!*

[P158]
Drip. Drip.

[P159]
Drops of blood fell from my tightly clenched fist. My throat burned as though I had swallowed a fireball.

[P160]
Just as I struggled to hold back the curses threatening to burst out, someone’s voice pierced my ears.

[P161]
“There is a way.”

[P162]
I opened my eyes and saw the boy’s face. Mungyeong continued, looking more serious than I had ever seen him.

[P163]
“Let us go to the Sichuan Tang Clan.”

[P164]
The Divine Physician looked at his Disciple with a dark expression.

[P165]
“Mungyeong. As you know, this Formless Ultimate Poison…”

[P166]
“I know, Master. I clearly remember you saying that the Tang Clan’s poison arts focus on killing and that their detoxification techniques are lacking. But…”

[P167]
Mungyeong looked straight at me with clear eyes.

[P168]
“If the Sichuan Tang Clan possesses the legendary sacred artifact said to detoxify any poison under heaven, then it may be possible.”

[P169]
Ding.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 343

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃343화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|휘오오오오.
  6|
  7|“바람 오지게 부네. 시부럴 거.”
  8|
  9|나는 가죽옷을 뚫고 들어오는 혹한의 추위에 몸을 부르르 떨었다. 한서불침(寒暑不侵)은 개뿔이, 한서매우침이다.
 10|
 11|“푸헹취!”
 12|
 13|이건 또 무슨 요상한 소린가 싶어 돌아보니 혁무진이 파래진 콧잔등을 문지르고 있었다.
 14|
 15|시선이 마주치자 녀석의 눈동자가 갈고리 모양으로 휘어진다.
 16|
 17|“왜요, 뭐요.”
 18|
 19|“…….”
 20|
 21|“뭘 봐요.”
 22|
 23|“아니, 난 그저 재채기 소리가 신기해서…….”
 24|
 25|“참나, 별 걸 다 신기해하시네. 그럴 시간 있으면 약초라도 하나 더 캐십쇼.”
 26|
 27|“……알았어. 내가 미안해.”
 28|
 29|슬그머니 시선을 피한 나는 근처에 있는 약초를 찾아 두리번거렸다.
 30|
 31|한빙지 채집 노예로 취직한 지 어느덧 닷새. 우리 사이의 상하 관계는 이미 역전된 지 오래였다.
 32|
 33|“아, 뭐 하세요. 저기 하나 있잖아요. 저기!”
 34|
 35|“어어, 그러네.”
 36|
 37|“정신 좀 똑바로 차리십쇼!”
 38|
 39|어후, 저걸 한 대 쥐어박을 수도 없고.
 40|
 41|친구 따라 강남 갔으면 땅값이라도 올랐을 텐데, 날 따라서 한빙지에 온 혁무진은 역대급 개고생을 하고 있었다.
 42|
 43|지금까지 온갖 싸움에 휘말려도 몇 번 투덜거리고 말던 녀석이 눈에 쌍심지를 켜고 노려볼 정도니 말 다 했지.
 44|
 45|“저는 저쪽 언덕 너머에서 약초 캘 테니까. 쉬지 마시고 계속하세요. 틈틈이 와서 볼 겁니다.”
 46|
 47|“……알았어, 인마.”
 48|
 49|참을 인(忍)을 되새긴 나는 눈을 살살 파헤친 다음 약초 하나를 쑥 뽑아 들었다.
 50|
 51|뒤이어 악덕 고용주, 아니 신의가 채집 노예들에게 일괄 지급한 망태기에 집어넣자 시스템 알림이 울린다.
 52|
 53|띠링.
 54|
 55|
 56|
 57|- [한빙초]를 채집했습니다.
 58|
 59|- 현재 남은 수량 [100 / 100].
 60|
 61|- [한빙초] 채집을 모두 완료했습니다!
 62|
 63|
 64|
 65|“후우. 드디어 또 하나 끝냈고.”
 66|
 67|슬슬 끝이 보인다는 게 한 줄기 위안이다.
 68|
 69|남은 수량을 파악하기 위해 퀘스트 창을 확인하는 내게 궁기방이 몸을 덜덜 떨며 다가왔다.
 70|
 71|“어, 얼마나 남았냐?”
 72|
 73|“한 이백 뿌리 정도. 잘하면 오늘 중에 끝날 것도 같은데?”
 74|
 75|“이백 뿌리나 남았다고?”
 76|
 77|“이백 뿌리밖에 안 남은 거지. 조금만 더 힘내.”
 78|
 79|“아니. 이백 뿌리는 너무 많아. 그리고 그때쯤이면 난 동사(凍死)한 시체가 되어 이 눈 어딘가에 파묻혀 있겠지.”
 80|
 81|“…….”
 82|
 83|지랄하네.
 84|
 85|오들오들 떨던 궁기방이 품에서 화섭자(火攝子)를 꺼내 불을 붙였다.
 86|
 87|미약한 불꽃을 향해 바짝 얼굴을 가져댄 녀석이 아련한 목소리로 중얼거렸다.
 88|
 89|“사부님이 보고 싶다. 따뜻한 객잔 앞 골목에 앉아 구걸하던 그때가 그리워…….”
 90|
 91|성냥팔이 소녀인가.
 92|
 93|나는 녀석의 행태에 기가 차서 중얼거렸다.
 94|
 95|“그때도 거지였으면서.”
 96|
 97|“적어도 그때는 따뜻한 거지였다. 추운 거지보다는 백 배 낫지.”
 98|
 99|“……그건 그러네.”
100|
101|“그때로 돌아가고 싶구나. 나른한 정오, 내리쬐는 햇살. 먹음직스럽게 걸어가는 황구…….”
102|
103|먹음직스러운 황구는 또 뭐야.
104|
105|동물보호단체가 기함할 소리를 한 궁기방의 눈꺼풀이 천천히 아래를 향해 내려갔다.
106|
107|이 자식이 설마?
108|
109|“야, 야!”
110|
111|나는 황급히 녀석의 몸에 열양지기를 흘려보냈다.
112|
113|이렇게라도 정신을 차려야…….
114|

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
